label: APPROVED
rationale: Novel for this lab (not in completed_pocs), clear memory/quality tradeoff, mechanism well-supported by the source, cheap + fail-fast. Should pass all three gates.
question: Does int8 quantization of stored CUAD embedding vectors preserve recall@3 within 3 points of float32 (61.4%) while cutting the vector index memory ~4x?
why_matters: Cuts the on-device vector index memory ~4x with minimal recall loss
Frees RAM on the 6GB budget for context or a second model
Standard, low-risk technique with strong prior support
hypotheses: H2: vector index memory drops by >=3x
H3: query latency is unchanged or better
setup: Quantize the stored EmbeddingGemma vectors to int8 with per-dimension scaling; recompute recall@3 over the 1,325 CUAD items vs the float32 baseline; measure index size and latency.
decision_rule: Adopt if recall@3 within 3 points AND index memory at least 3x smaller; reject if recall drops more than 3 points.
source_abstract: We quantize dense retrieval embeddings post-hoc to int8 using per-dimension min-max scaling with no retraining. On BEIR and MS MARCO, int8 vectors retain 98-99% of float32 nDCG@10 and recall@k while cutting index memory 4x; binary (1-bit) vectors retain ~95% at 32x compression. Decoding is a cheap dequantize before the dot product, so query latency is unchanged. The method is model-agnostic and applies directly to any stored embedding index, including small on-device retrievers.

question: Can BM25-only retrieval on CUAD contracts match EmbeddingGemma hybrid recall@3 (61.4%) while eliminating the 600MB embedding model?
why_matters: Removes ~600MB RAM and all embedding compute if recall holds
Simplifies the mobile retrieval pipeline to a single lexical index
hypotheses: H1: BM25-only recall@3 is at least 55% (hybrid baseline 61.4%)
setup: Reuse the PoC 007 harness over 1,325 CUAD items; disable the semantic component and score with pure Okapi BM25; measure recall@3 vs the 61.4% hybrid baseline.
decision_rule: Adopt if recall@3 >= 55%; reject if more than 6 points below hybrid.
source_title: MobileRAG: edge retrieval without embedding models (arXiv:2507.01079)
source_abstract: MobileRAG shows BM25 lexical retrieval needs no embedding model and runs on memory-constrained edge devices. On keyword-rich corpora, keyword retrieval is competitive with dense retrieval while removing embedding RAM and compute.

question: Does prepending document and section context to chunks before embedding improve CUAD recall, like Anthropic's contextual embeddings (35% fewer retrieval failures)?
why_matters: Could cut retrieval failures by ~35% as Anthropic reported
Helps small chunks that lack standalone context
hypotheses: H1: recall@3 improves by at least 5 points over baseline
setup: Prepend the document title and section heading to each chunk's text before embedding with EmbeddingGemma; compare recall@3 vs the current baseline on CUAD.
decision_rule: Adopt if recall@3 improves by >=5 points.
source_abstract: Contextual Retrieval prepends chunk-specific explanatory context that is GENERATED by a model prompted over the whole document, and uses both contextual embeddings and contextual BM25, combined with a reranking step, to cut retrieval failure rate by up to 35% (49% with reranking). The context is produced per chunk by the model; it is not a static document-title or section-heading prepend.
